claims.text: A defect-inclusive predictive model will more closely match measured thermal conductivity than conventional defect-free analytical models.
The relevant material is bulk, typically polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed model is trained on experimental data and defect-inclusive simulations.
The proposed prediction applies in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature regimes.
One weight percent oxygen induces defect states and lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced defect states and lattice distortions modify phonon scattering.
Oxygen-induced defect states and lattice distortions modify electron scattering.
Traditional perfect-crystal analytical models neglect oxygen-impurity scattering and associated transport modifications.
Representing realistic defect structures allows the proposed model to adjust thermal-transport predictions for impurity-enhanced scattering.
The defect-inclusive model is expected to predict thermal conductivity within ±5% of experimental measurements.
Conventional defect-free analytical approaches typically have thermal-conductivity errors of 10% or more.
The proposed model will have a significantly lower prediction error than conventional defect-free analytical approaches.
Applicability is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The exact error reduction may depend on defect-interaction complexity and experimental uncertainty.
